Mars Maps — Interplanetary Survival Guide

Mars Maps is an interactive 3D and 2D Mars navigation platform for exploration, education, and future mission-planning concepts.

Key Features
•⁠  ⁠Synchronized 3D globe and zoomable 2D Mars map
•⁠  ⁠Landmark search and Free Roam exploration mode
•⁠  ⁠English and Turkish interface and landmark descriptions
•⁠  ⁠Separate selectable NASA data layers
•⁠  ⁠Terrain-aware route candidates with route markers on both maps
•⁠  ⁠Vehicle type and cargo-weight route settings
NASA Data Used

Mars Maps integrates NASA MOLA topography, Viking global imagery, CTX imagery, Mars Odyssey GRS composition data, and TES thermal-inertia maps.

Route Safety Approach

The PHP route system considers elevation, slope, local relief, vehicle type, and cargo weight. It clearly marks chemical, radiation, and heat hazards as unassessed when reliable mission-safe thresholds are unavailable, rather than making unsafe assumptions.

Goal

Our goal is to make complex NASA Mars data accessible through a cohesive map experience that helps users understand Mars as a real, explorable world.
details:
Project Details — Mars Maps

Overview

Mars Maps is an interactive Mars exploration and navigation website designed as a “Google Maps for Mars” experience. It helps users explore Mars through a realistic 3D globe and a synchronized, zoomable 2D map. The project transforms NASA planetary data into a visual tool that is easier for students, explorers, and future mission-planning teams to understand.

The website is available in English and Turkish and is designed to be visually seamless, simple to use, and scientifically responsible.

Main Features

Mars Maps includes a 3D Mars globe with realistic Mars surface colors, terrain displacement, and normal-map lighting based on elevation data. Users can rotate, zoom, and inspect Mars while avoiding excessive zoom levels that would reveal low-resolution imagery.

The 2D map is fully interactive and synchronized with the 3D globe. When users move, zoom, select a location, or create a route on one map, the other map updates accordingly. This allows users to use the 2D map for practical navigation while still seeing the larger planetary context in 3D.

Users can search for coordinates, landmarks, landing regions, craters, volcanoes, plains, and canyon systems. Free Roam mode includes clickable landmark indicators, labels that remain readable on screen, landmark descriptions in English and Turkish, NASA source links, and available NASA imagery. Examples include Jezero Crater, Perseverance’s landing site, Gale Crater, Olympus Mons, Valles Marineris, Gusev Crater, Hellas Planitia, and Elysium Planitia.

NASA Data Layers

Scientific datasets remain separate instead of being merged into one misleading map. Users can select and compare:

  • Viking global Mars surface imagery 
  • MOLA elevation and color-shaded topography 
  • CTX grayscale surface imagery 
  • Water-equivalent hydrogen abundance 
  • Chlorine abundance 
  • Night thermal inertia 
  • Day thermal-inertia visualization

Each layer includes NASA source attribution and explanatory notes. The project also avoids presenting non-georeferenced radiation illustrations or temperature images as precise navigation maps.

Route Planning and Safety Assessment

Users can select a start point and destination, choose a vehicle type, enter cargo weight, and request a terrain-aware route candidate. The PHP routing system considers numerical elevation, slope, local relief, travel distance, and vehicle/cargo limits. It returns route points, route distance, elevation gain, sampled slope, estimated travel time, and the data resolution used.

Routes are shown on both the 3D globe and 2D map with visible dots and smooth route lines. The route planner includes walking, rover, truck, and crew-rover profiles. For example, light walking routes use a conservative rise/run = 0.8 slope limit.

A hazard-assessment panel allows users to choose which hazards they want reported. However, Mars Maps responsibly explains that water, chlorine, thermal inertia, radiation, and heat cannot currently be used as fully validated safe/unsafe route barriers. The system never claims that missing scientific data means an area is safe.

Technology Used

  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript 
  • Three.js for the 3D Mars globe 
  • PHP for the routing API and terrain calculations 
  • Docker and Render for deployment 
  • NASA Mars Trek, NASA PDS, NASA/JPL, MOLA, Viking, CTX, Mars Odyssey GRS, and TES datasets 
  • Custom numerical terrain raster handling, route-search logic, map synchronization, translations, and audio controls

Creativity and Intended Impact

Mars Maps combines scientific visualization, user-friendly navigation, and responsible safety communication. Rather than showing Mars as a static image, it presents the planet as an explorable environment where users can compare terrain, resources, surface conditions, and travel challenges.

Our goal is to make NASA Mars data more accessible, encourage curiosity about planetary science, and demonstrate how future explorers might use layered geographic information to understand routes and conditions on another world.
